name: Judge pass rate over the chat quality cases
scoped_purpose: Judge pass rate over the chat_quality datasets on a disposable dev world: hard deterministic pre-checks first (reply text, routing, side effects, tools called), then a model judge against the case rubric and the named pivot facts. Offline validity arm (reference_replies): each case validates and its deterministic pre-checks accept a reference reply and reject an empty one
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of each implementation on the same cases, with the recorded cost as the tie-break; each run is one row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash, and the leaderboard compares rows only when the hash matches.
gap: The graded arm is recorded on a stratified sample drawn in process at the cheapest tier, and it passes few of the sampled cases: the headline is that the chat misses the rubric on most of them, not that the metric is unsound. The recorded misses repeat: it asks which quest, or for data the quest already holds, instead of inferring the quest or reading the seeded values; it proposes instead of writing when the request was unambiguous; it states a fact no read supports; and a multi-step request ends with a queued task and no report of what is unfinished. A case takes dozens of model calls, so the cost per passing turn is high at this pass rate, and no stronger tier has been run. Passing is judged against a rubric by claude -p and is not yet calibrated against Joshua's verdicts, and one case passed in one run and failed in the next, so a sample this small cannot rank two implementations. The recorded row points to a committed per-case file of the judge's reasons (evaluation/components/chat_quality/recorded/dev_quest_chat_sample.json), recovered from the judge cache for the sampled cases; one case has no verdict there because it failed a deterministic check before the judge ran, and its raw record was not kept. One recorded reason (a status check that errored inside the in-process transport) may be the harness rather than the chat. The offline arm covers every dataset case and says only that the metric is sound. A result ties to the brain version the dev backend serves. This metric is also the only one that sees whether a whole reply is grounded, so it has to carry the case for keeping the planner over a cheaper label-only router.
action: Run the same sample on the next tier up, and a larger sample, to answer the cost per passing turn. Fix the recurring misses (ask before inferring, propose instead of write, ungrounded facts, unfinished multi-step reports) and re-run the same sample. Confirm the rubric as the definition of a good reply and label a sample of verdicts so the judge can be calibrated.
